### CVE-2025-0241 — Memory corruption when using JavaScript Text Segmentation
- Assigner: mozilla | Published: 2025-01-07 | Updated: 2026-04-13 | Max CVSS: 7.7
- CWE: CWE-401 CWE-401 Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 7.7 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:L`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total

When segmenting specially crafted text, segmentation would corrupt memory leading to a potentially exploitable crash. This vulnerability was fixed in Firefox 134, Firefox ESR 128.6, Thunderbird 134, and Thunderbird 128.6.

Affected:
- Mozilla / Firefox: unaffected 128.6 <=128.* (rpm); unaffected 134 <=* (rpm)
- Mozilla / Thunderbird: unaffected 128.6 <=128.* (rpm); unaffected 134 <=* (rpm)

Credits: Nils Bars

References:

### CVE-2025-1930 — AudioIPC StreamData could trigger a use-after-free in the Browser process
- Assigner: mozilla | Published: 2025-03-04 | Updated: 2026-06-04 | Max CVSS: 8.8
- CWE: CWE-416 CWE-416 Use After Free
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 8.8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

On Windows, a compromised content process could use bad StreamData sent over AudioIPC to trigger a use-after-free in the Browser process. This could have led to a sandbox escape. This vulnerability was fixed in Firefox 136, Firefox ESR 115.21, Firefox ESR 128.8, Thunderbird 136, and Thunderbird 128.8.

Affected:

### CVE-2025-1933 — JIT corruption of WASM i32 return values on 64-bit CPUs
- Assigner: mozilla | Published: 2025-03-04 | Updated: 2026-06-04 | Max CVSS: 7.6
- CWE: CWE-noinfo Not enough information
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 7.6 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial

On 64-bit CPUs, when the JIT compiles WASM i32 return values they can pick up bits from left over memory. This can potentially cause them to be treated as a different type. This vulnerability was fixed in Firefox 136, Firefox ESR 115.21, Firefox ESR 128.8, Thunderbird 136, and Thunderbird 128.8.

Affected:
- Mozilla / Firefox: unaffected 115.21 <=115.* (rpm); unaffected 128.8 <=128.* (rpm); unaffected 136 <=* (rpm)
- Mozilla / Thunderbird: unaffected 128.8 <=128.* (rpm); unaffected 136 <=* (rpm)

Credits: Xiangwei Zhang and kkdong of Tencent Security YUNDING LAB

### CVE-2025-1936 — Adding %00 and a fake extension to a jar: URL  changed the interpretation of the contents
- Assigner: mozilla | Published: 2025-03-04 | Updated: 2026-04-13 | Max CVSS: 7.3
- CWE: CWE-158 CWE-158 Improper Neutralization of Null Byte or NUL Character
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 7.3 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:L`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

jar: URLs retrieve local file content packaged in a ZIP archive. The null and everything after it was ignored when retrieving the content from the archive, but the fake extension after the null was used to determine the type of content. This could have been used to hide code in a web extension disguised as something else like an image. This vulnerability was fixed in Firefox 136, Firefox ESR 128.8, Thunderbird 136, and Thunderbird 128.8.

Affected:
- Mozilla / Firefox: unaffected 128.8 <=128.* (rpm); unaffected 136 <=* (rpm)
- Mozilla / Thunderbird: unaffected 128.8 <=128.* (rpm); unaffected 136 <=* (rpm)

Credits: Surya Dev Singh

References:

- Assigner: mozilla | Published: 2025-05-14 | Updated: 2026-04-13 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: CWE-290 CWE-290 Authentication Bypass by Spoofing

Thunderbird parses addresses in a way that can allow sender spoofing in case the server allows an invalid From address to be used. This vulnerability was fixed in Thunderbird 128.10.1 and Thunderbird 138.0.1.

### CVE-2025-3909 — JavaScript Execution via Spoofed PDF Attachment and file:/// Link
- Assigner: mozilla | Published: 2025-05-14 | Updated: 2026-04-13 | Max CVSS: 8.1
- CWE: CWE-356 CWE-356 Product UI does not Warn User of Unsafe Actions
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 8.1 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Thunderbird's handling of the X-Mozilla-External-Attachment-URL header can be exploited to execute JavaScript in the file:/// context. By crafting a nested email attachment (message/rfc822) and setting its content type to application/pdf, Thunderbird may incorrectly render it as HTML when opened, allowing the embedded JavaScript to run without requiring a file download. This behavior relies on Thunderbird auto-saving the attachment to /tmp and linking to it via the file:/// protocol, potentially enabling JavaScript execution as part of the HTML. This vulnerability was fixed in Thunderbird 128.10.1 and Thunderbird 138.0.1.

Affected:
- Mozilla / Thunderbird: unaffected 128.10.1 <=128.* (rpm); unaffected 138.0.1 <=* (rpm)

Credits: Dario Weißer

References:
- https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1958376
- https://www.mozilla.org/security/advisories/mfsa2025-34/
- https://www.mozilla.org/security/advisories/mfsa2025-35/
- https://lists.debian.org/debian-lts-announce/2025/05/msg00022.html

### CVE-2025-6433 — WebAuthn would allow a user to sign a challenge on a webpage with an invalid TLS certificate

- CWE: CWE-295 CWE-295 Improper Certificate Validation
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 9.8 CRITICAL `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total

If a user visited a webpage with an invalid TLS certificate, and granted an exception, the webpage was able to provide a WebAuthn challenge that the user would be prompted to complete. ### CVE-2025-13465 — Prototype Pollution Vulnerability in Lodash _.unset and _.omit functions
- Assigner: openjs | Published: 2026-01-21 | Updated: 2026-10-15 | Max CVSS: 8.2
- CWE: CWE-1321 CWE-1321: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes ('Prototype Pollution'); CWE-1321 Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes ('Prototype Pollution')
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 6.9 MEDIUM `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:L/VA:L/SC:H/SI:H/SA:H/E:P`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial
- CVSS 3.1 (redhat-SADP): 8.2 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:H`

The _.unset and _.omit functions in Lodash are vulnerable to prototype pollution. An attacker can pass crafted paths which cause Lodash to delete methods from global prototypes. The issue permits deletion of properties but does not allow overwriting their original behavior. The issue is patched from 4.17.23 to 4.18.0 depending on the package: lodash, lodash-es, and lodash-amd in 4.17.23, and the standalone lodash.unset and lodash.omit packages in 4.18.0.

Affected:
- Lodash / lodash: affected 4.0.0 <4.17.23 (semver); unaffected 4.17.23 (semver)
- Lodash / lodash-amd: affected 4.0.0 <4.17.23 (semver); unaffected 4.17.23 (semver)
- Lodash / lodash-es: affected 4.0.0 <4.17.23 (semver); unaffected 4.17.23 (semver)
- Lodash / lodash.unset: affected 4.0.0 <4.18.0 (semver); unaffected 4.18.0 (semver)
- Lodash / lodash.omit: affected 4.0.0 <4.18.0 (semver); unaffected 4.18.0 (semver)
